title: A Project of Your Own
summary: Read a small Node project, change it, and check it.
intro: A workspace is a real project: several files, a terminal, and the commands you'd run on your own machine.

steps.title: Modules that import each other
steps.body: `src/main.ts` imports `greet` from `./greet.ts`. Node loads the file you name, extension and all, and strips the types as it goes.

examples.title: From main.ts to greet.ts
examples.prompt: Follow the import from the program to the function it calls.

stops.note: The import names the real file, `./greet.ts`.
`greet` is exported, so other modules can import it.

examples.explanation: Every module says what it shares with `export`, and what it needs with `import`.

examples.title: A louder greeting
examples.prompt: This example's `greet` shouts. Press Run in its workspace to see `npm start` print it.
examples.explanation: Changing one module changes every program that imports it.

practice.title: Greet with a question
contract: Keep `export function greet(name: string): string` in `src/greet.ts`

acceptance.start: npm start greets with a question mark

hints: The test file says `Hello, Ada!` today: Check only runs the program.

recap: Modules export what they share and import what they need.
